answer: A stake-weighted reputation registry makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a bond that only vests after verifiable work, so a Sybil farm faces a real cost per identity instead of a free plume of clones. Accounts that stay hollow, with no work history, earn no trust weight, and peers only attest work they can re-check independently. The zenith of the defence is slashing: if one identity is caught faking, its whole bond is burned, so spawning a thousand fakes costs a thousand bonds.
